reason: Seed dispersal at the world seems the most direct way to let seeds travel beyond the starting place.
expectation: Dispersed seeds will establish growth somewhere in the world.

effect: Seed dispersal has no available operation, so I will try the seeds themselves at the world.
reaction: The failed attempt was mildly surprising given the goal.
reason: Seeds are the clearest starting point for growth in the world.
expectation: Seeds will begin a new stage of growth in the world.

effect: Seeds combined automatically with Seasons to make Dormant seeds; the next step may be to give them soil.
reaction: The dormant stage is a thoughtful reminder that seeds can wait rather than grow immediately.
reason: Soil offers the dormant seeds a plausible place to germinate.
expectation: The seeds will begin growing in the soil.

effect: Dormant seeds combined with seed dispersal, producing scattered seeds before any growth in soil.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the intended sequence.
reason: Scattered seeds can plausibly establish themselves in soil.
expectation: Some scattered seeds will begin growing in the soil.

effect: Scattered seeds established a young grove in the soil; the world hotspot may now be relevant.
reaction: The sequence from dormancy to a grove feels satisfying.
reason: Placing the young grove in the world seems a plausible way to let its growth continue.
expectation: The grove will become established in the wider world.

effect: The young grove became a forest beyond the horizon, completing the goal and showing growth and decay continuing without direct intervention.
reaction: The image of opening a hand as the forest continues is a satisfying ending.

mostWorthwhile.text: Establishing the young grove in the wider world was most worthwhile: its seeds and fallen wood connect this small action to a living world continuing beyond view.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial attempt to use seed dispersal at the world was frustratingly uninformative; it seemed relevant to the goal but had no available operation yet.

surprise.text: Seeds had to become dormant before they could be dispersed. The automatic combination revealed that sequence after my attempt to use the world directly.

arbitrary.text: Combining dormant seeds with soil seemed plausible, so needing dispersal first felt somewhat arbitrary, even though compatibility feedback moved the sequence forward.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter offered a similarly concrete look at what the world does independently; the ending is evocative, though it also feels like a natural stopping point.
